scope_groups.header: Site Electrical & Low Voltage Systems - Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete Scope of Work per plans and specifications. This Scope of Work shall include, but not be limited to:
items: Safe-off and disconnect existing electrical and low voltage equipment scheduled for demolition, including the concessions building, press box panel, field lighting and scoreboard.
Salvage the sports field loudspeakers, PA system cabinet, wireless transmitter and microphones prior to demolition; coordinate removal and storage with Contractor.
Supply and install the new site transformer, Musco lighting controller and weatherproof enclosures as indicated.
Coordinate transformer mounting requirements with Scoreboard Subcontractor.
Includes power and data connections to the field lighting, scoreboard, press box and irrigation controller.
Includes Low Voltage pathway from the existing field in-ground boxes back to the High School IT Room, including conduit, fiber and CAT6A cabling.
Includes exterior wall-mounted weatherproof pull boxes and patch cables for the Low Voltage pathway, as specified.
Includes sawcutting, patch-back and repair as required at the existing High School building, to match existing finishes.
Coordinate work at the existing High School building with Contractor and Owner.
Coordinate layout of sleeves, block-outs and embedded items with Masonry and Concrete Subcontractors.

scope_groups.header: Elementary School Electrical Demolition - Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete Scope of Work per plans and specifications. This Scope of Work shall include, but not be limited to:
items: Safe-off and disconnect electrical and low voltage systems, including fire alarm systems and feeders, at the Elementary School buildings scheduled for demolition.
Coordinate demolition sequencing with the Abatement & Building Wrecking Subcontractor.

scope_groups.header: Trenching, Excavation & Foundations - Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete Scope of Work per plans and specifications. This Scope of Work shall include, but not be limited to:
items: Includes hard-dig excavation, including Caliche, for all trenching and foundations under this Scope of Work.
Includes trenching for Landscape Irrigation control power.
Includes excavation, reinforcing, concrete, anchor bolts and drypack for the 4 Musco sports field light pole foundations, per Musco's precast base.
Assumes spoils generated by this Scope of Work may be stockpiled on site; offsite haul-off is excluded.
Coordinate underground piping location and depth with the Concrete Subcontractor to minimize sleeving.
Coordinate site utility layout with the Earthwork and Landscape & Irrigation Subcontractors.

scope_groups.header: Sports Field Lighting - Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete Scope of Work per plans and specifications. This Scope of Work shall include, but not be limited to:
items: Supply and install the Musco sports field lighting system, including poles, luminaires, conduit and wiring, per the Lighting Fixture Schedule.
Includes footing design for the sports field light poles, coordinated with Musco's precast base and reinforcing.
Includes a photometric light study showing footcandle coverage across the field and track.
Includes programming and commissioning of the Musco lighting control system.

scope_groups.header: Building Electrical - Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete Scope of Work per plans and specifications. This Scope of Work shall include, but not be limited to:
items: Includes all panels, receptacles, switches, and interior and exterior lighting and lighting controls as scheduled.
Includes exterior emergency light fixtures as required by code, whether or not shown on the drawings.
Provide a light fixture in every room, whether or not shown on the drawings.
Includes temporary power to the jobsite, 200A at the trailer yard and 200A at the new building.
Includes power and control wiring to the electric operator at the coiling counter shutter, Door 106A, per Door Hardware Set #4/#5.
Coordinate ceiling-mounted fixture layout with HVAC and Acoustical Ceiling Subcontractors, centered in the acoustical tile.
Includes final electrical connections to food service equipment and Owner-furnished, Owner-installed equipment.
Includes final connections to Mechanical and Plumbing equipment and to smoke detectors.
Includes a 120V power circuit for controls at each equipment controller, whether or not shown on the drawings.
Supply only, F.O.B. jobsite, access doors and panels for concealed electrical work, keyed alike; installation by Framing Subcontractor.

scope_groups.header: Low Voltage, Communications, Audio-Visual & Security Systems - Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete Scope of Work per plans and specifications. This Scope of Work shall include, but not be limited to:
items: Includes low voltage systems in the Concessions Building, Press Box and Ticket Booth.
Install Owner Furnished, Contractor Installed (OFCI) low voltage equipment, including salvaged equipment, as indicated.
Includes final low voltage connections to equipment furnished by others.
Includes conduit pathway and mule tape stubbed for future fire alarm, per plans.
Supply and install the CCTV video management system and video storage, and install Owner-provided cameras and mounts.
Includes reinstallation and final connections for the salvaged sports field sound and paging equipment in the new Press Box.
Coordinate Audio-Visual final connections with the Press Box manufacturer.
Provide a qualified representative on-site for all tests and inspections, and coordinate scheduling with inspectors for final approval.
Complete final utility adjustments prior to site concrete placement.
Seal all through-wall and through-floor penetrations with acoustical sealant.
Coordinate roof penetrations with Roofing Subcontractor; space penetrations a minimum of 12 inches apart.
Coordinate electrical testing and commissioning requirements with Owner's consultant.
Coordinate with HVAC & Building Controls Subcontractor for interface with the Building Control Systems.
Where raceways are architecturally exposed, install in a neat, aesthetic manner and mock up as directed by the Superintendent.

GMP BackSheet lines #105 Specialty Low Voltage Systems, #106 Electronic Safety & Security Systems, and #107 Sports Field Lighting all carry $0 and point back to line #103 -- confirming this one subcontract carries power, field lighting, low voltage, communications, and security together, consistent with the Scope of Work narrative's own structure.
_amount_buildup: Base Bid - Quantum Electric Homework Response R4 (06.01.26)
ADD Alternate 05 - Electrical excavation, 100% hard dig
ADD Alternate 06 - Concrete foundations for (4) Musco poles (excavation priced under Alternate 05)
ADD Alternate 103.01 - Electrical Demo at Abandoned Elementary School Campus
DEDUCT Alternate 03 - Remove Showlight & RGBW option from Musco poles
_amount_note: No single document states this buildup narratively. It is reconstructed from Quantum's own alternate pricing in Homework Response R4 (base $937,714; Alt 05 +$71,516; Alt 06 +$33,102; Alt 103.01 +$41,564; Deductive Alt 03 -$9,355) and sums to $1,074,541 exactly -- matching the GMP BackSheet's carried value to the dollar. Two alternates offered in the same document (Deductive Alt 04, remove Press Box lights/receptacles/circuits, -$6,144; Deductive Alt 07/08, remove the Low Voltage pathway and fiber to the High School, -$37,069/-$48,702) do NOT appear in the reconciliation, meaning Press Box electrical and the High School Low Voltage pathway are both carried IN at full scope. See _open_pm_items -- this reconstruction needs PM confirmation before issue.

cover_sheet.project_name: NCSD - Tonopah HS Sports Field Replacement

_cover_sheet_note: Material procurement and start dates left unset so the cover sheet prints CONFIRM. RFP-103 carries three separate schedule chains in the buyout log (electrical lighting package need 07.06.27; Musco light fixtures need 03.08.27; electrical rough-in need 02.08.27) with no single unambiguous field date to print here. P&P bond rate 1.7% taken from the pre-award leveling tab (BP103); no document states the bond is priced separately or excluded, unlike Henderson Masonry's proposal on RFP-031, so it is assumed included in the carried price.
_open_pm_items: GMP-08 (new) -- The carried $1,074,541 reconciles exactly to Quantum's base $937,714 plus Alternates 05 (+$71,516, 100% hard dig), 06 (+$33,102, concrete foundations for 4 Musco poles) and 103.01 (+$41,564, Elementary School electrical demo), less Deductive Alternate 03 (-$9,355, remove Musco RGBW/Showlight). No document states this buildup narratively -- it is reconstructed from the arithmetic. Confirm before issue.

Musco's own 05.11.26 email (day before bid opening) states the drawn pole foundation detail predates the added track-lighting fixtures and the geotechnical report, and that structural is now calling for a reinforced precast base with a rebar cage that 'none of the contractors are including in their bid.' Confirm whether the accepted $33,102 (Alternate 06) reflects the updated reinforced design or the outdated one bidders priced against.

Quantum's 05.20.26 scope-review agenda states 'Excludes patch-backs and paint for existing building tie-in,' contradicting Scope of Work #103's express requirement to sawcut, patch back and match existing finishes at the High School tie-in. The exhibit carries the Scope of Work's position (per the authority hierarchy, proposals never relieve a sub of the contract documents) -- flag and confirm before issue.

The Basis of GMP excludes 'Active Network Equipment (Servers, Switches, etc.)' project-wide, but Section 27 00 00 para 1.1.A.1 expressly requires the Contractor to furnish and install network switches and associated UPS -- a direct document conflict. The exhibit follows the GMP exclusion per the 08.04.26 ruling that Exhibit B supersedes as an addendum. Confirm who supplies switches (District IT, or a separate buy) before issue.

Per the buyout log (08.07.26): 'the ASI formalizing the no-fire-alarm direction has not issued; the GMP Exclusion covers the money but not the drawings.' E0-01 (notes 80-82) and E3-00 (sheet note 3) still carry live fire-alarm language and a drawn future-fire-alarm conduit stub. The exhibit carries the pathway/mule-tape stub and excludes the system itself, consistent with the GMP exclusion, but the drawings have not been formally revised to match.

Section 08 71 00 Door Hardware (added by Addendum #1) is cited for RFP-103's electrified hardware. The only documented electrified item found is the Door 106A coiling counter shutter (electric push-button operation, Hardware Sets #4/#5); Quantum's 06.01.26 email confirms it will 'just take care of it' at no separate cost. Confirm no other electrified hardware exists on this project before issue -- the separate Door 106 panic-hardware ambiguity (GMP-02) is tracked under ITB-054/ITB-056, not here.

Homework Response R4 is titled 'Delete LV Pathway to HS,' and its own Deductive Alternates 07 and 08 price removing the Low Voltage pathway and fiber to the High School IT Room -- but neither deduct appears in the reconciliation that reaches the carried $1,074,541. The pathway is carried IN, per the Scope of Work narrative. Flagging so the misleading filename does not cause the pathway to be dropped at buyout.

Musco fixture types F1-RGBW and F2-RGBW are shown on the Lighting Fixture Schedule (E0-02) but are removed from the carried price by Deductive Alternate 03. Confirm the Owner is aware the drawn RGBW/show-lighting feature is not included.
Confirm RFP-030's concrete scope does not also claim the 4 Musco sports field light pole foundations now carried under RFP-103 (per Alternate 06) -- avoid a double-claim between packages.

review_appendix._purpose: PM request 08.11.26. Rule 14 strips every obligation the specs and drawings already carry. This lists what was stripped so the PM can put any of it back. Draft only -- build with --final to suppress it.
intro: Rule 14 keeps out of this exhibit anything the Contract Documents already state, so the Subcontract carries one copy of each obligation rather than two that can drift.

Every line below was drafted, verified and then removed on that basis. All of them still bind the Subcontractor through the document named beneath them. Tick any that should be restated in the Scope of Work above.
